| _October 28, 2026_ |  
  
Dear Hiring Manager,

I'm excited to apply for the Senior Full Stack Engineer role on Northwind Health's NBA platform team. The work you're describing — a control plane for authoring, governing, and publishing member actions across an enterprise — is exactly the kind of system I find most interesting to build: one where correctness, state integrity, and usability have to coexist under real operational pressure.

At Rice University, I've spent four-plus years as the primary Salesforce architect and developer for an IT department serving nearly 10,000 active users. That means designing data models, building APIs, managing CI/CD pipelines, and translating messy business workflows into clean, governed experiences — the same combination this role calls for. I've built Lightning Web Components in JavaScript, managed complex approval flows and lifecycle states across 60+ automations, and architected secure authentication patterns including guest login with temporary key rotation to avoid unnecessary license exposure. Those problems map directly to the action lifecycle, versioning, and governance challenges you're describing.

On the full-stack side, I've built React and React Native applications backed by PostgreSQL, deployed cloud functions on AWS Lambda, and integrated AWS Bedrock for LLM-powered features. I'm fluent in TypeScript and bring a strong testing and code-review discipline shaped by coursework in software architecture and algorithms at Georgia Tech (MS CS, 4.0 GPA). My Community Center Rentals project is a close analogue to the work here: a Next.js/TypeScript application with a Neon PostgreSQL backend, Upstash Redis for ephemeral state and race-safe locking, role-based access control, and an audit log on every mutating action — built precisely to be reliable under concurrent load.

I don't currently have production Kafka experience, and I'll be straightforward about that. But my background in event-driven state management, PostgreSQL schema design, and CI/CD-driven deployments gives me a solid foundation to come up to speed quickly on the streaming layer.

I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can contribute to the NBA platform team.

---
  
Sincerely,  
  
David Hanks, P.E.
resume:
# David Hanks, P.E.
| david@example.com | [linkedin.com/in/example](https://www.linkedin.com/in/example) | (555) 010-0199 |
|-------------------|:-----------------------------:|--------------:|

Full-stack engineer with 5+ years building production React/TypeScript applications, PostgreSQL-backed APIs, and cloud-native services on AWS. Brings deep Salesforce platform ownership, CI/CD pipelines, and enterprise workflow design to complex, user-facing operational systems.

---

## Professional Experience

### Full Stack Engineer — Rice University *(Feb 2021 – Present | Remote)*
- Architected and own Rice IT's Salesforce platform: ~10,000 active users, 60+ flows, 3 digital experience sites, and 4 major production applications — designing data models, APIs, and role-based access controls end-to-end.
- Developed and shipped features using Apex, Lightning Web Components (JavaScript), and SOQL; translated complex HR and IT workflows into governed, configurable user experiences.
- Built and maintained CI/CD Bitbucket pipelines to test and deploy version-controlled software to Salesforce, enforcing code-review gates before production releases.
- Architected a secure guest-login pattern using temporary rotating keys to avoid single-use community licenses — an identity and access design analogous to OAuth token flows.
- Developed an automated, containerized daily backup of custom objects; configured OAuth-authenticated connected apps for backup, VCS pipeline, and data-integration services.
- Maintained and patched cloud APIs (Python/Flask), WAF, CDNs, and DNS; collaborated with Oracle/Banner teams to keep employee and student data synchronized across systems.

---

## Education

**Georgia Institute of Technology** — M.S. Computer Science | GPA: 4.0 | Dec 2023  
**University of Louisiana at Lafayette** — B.S. Mechanical Engineering | GPA: 3.4 | 2002

## Personal Projects

### Community Center Rentals
A two-app Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript system for online facility reservations. Features a public storefront (browse, check availability, pay via PayPal) and an authenticated admin app with server-side RBAC (scheduler vs. admin roles), an audit log on every mutating request, and a race-safe booking layer — Neon PostgreSQL advisory locks plus a transaction-level re-check ensure no double-booking under concurrent load. Ephemeral state (pending orders, locks, webhook dedup) lives in Upstash Redis with short TTLs. Both apps deploy to GCP Cloud Run (scale-to-zero) with secrets in Secret Manager.
**Technologies:** Next.js, TypeScript, Neon PostgreSQL, Upstash Redis, Firebase Auth, PayPal, GCP Cloud Run, Secret Manager

*(No public URL on file for this project — omitted per instructions)*

### Climbing Pins
React Native mobile app for discovering and sharing rock climbing routes on an interactive map. Global state is driven by Cloud Firestore `onSnapshot` listeners streaming live data into a React Context store. Features dual Firebase backend fan-out (Firestore + Realtime Database) through a coordination middleware layer, geohash-based proximity queries, Firebase Auth with custom claims for admin/moderator RBAC, and Android runtime permissions for camera, media, and location. Released to the Google Play Store. [read more...](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL8KBlR63foXz7Sw3mzJc6e9Dy5FmX8Jcy&si=qDIWACxDcfe-iyBf)

---

---

recommendations.gaps:
- **Node.js/Fastify standalone REST API services (hard requirement):** David's backend APIs are Python (Flask/Django) and Salesforce Apex. TypeScript appears in Next.js server-side routes but not in dedicated Node.js microservice/REST API development — a core daily-driver skill for this role.
- **Kafka and event-driven architecture (listed as a workflow integration requirement, preferred but operationally central):** No Kafka experience in the master resume. The posting describes Kafka-based publishing as a primary integration pattern for the action pipeline — partial match only via general understanding of async/event patterns.
- **TanStack Router, Query, Form, Table (preferred):** David's React work uses standard patterns; no TanStack-specific library experience documented.
- **Fastify, Prisma, or Drizzle ORM (preferred):** Not present. His ORM-adjacent work is SQLAlchemy-style raw queries and Salesforce SOQL — transferable concept, but not the named tools.
- **Kubernetes, Azure DevOps, ArgoCD (preferred):** CI/CD experience is Bitbucket Pipelines and GCP Cloud Run; no Kubernetes or Azure DevOps exposure documented — minor gap for preferred qualifications only.
- **Healthcare/HIPAA/PHI compliance (preferred):** No documented experience in a regulated healthcare or insurance environment — a soft differentiator the posting mentions but does not list as required.

---
recommendations.strengths:
- **5+ years full-stack engineering + React:** Professional software career began Feb 2021 at Rice; React used in GPS Tracker, Climbing Pins (React Native), and Community Center Rentals (Next.js/TypeScript) — all production-deployed.
- **PostgreSQL schema design & data modeling:** Community Center Rentals features a race-safe Neon PostgreSQL reservation schema with advisory locks, transaction-level re-checks, and support for both unique and fungible inventory — directly analogous to reliable action state modeling.
- **Enterprise workflow design with governance & versioning:** Sole architect of Rice's Salesforce platform with 60+ lifecycle flows, approval processes, configurable applications, and RBAC — maps to Action Library authoring, configuration, and governance requirements.
- **CI/CD pipelines:** Built and maintains Bitbucket CI/CD pipelines with code-review gates deploying to Salesforce; containerized backup and connected-app deployments show familiarity with automated, repeatable delivery.
- **RBAC and identity/access patterns:** Architected secure guest login with rotating temporary keys at Rice; implemented server-side role checks (scheduler vs. admin) in Community Center Rentals — adjacent to OAuth 2.0/RBAC preferred qualifications.
- **TypeScript + Next.js full-stack:** Community Center Rentals is built entirely in TypeScript with Next.js App Router, Neon PostgreSQL, and Upstash Redis — demonstrates the strongly typed, contract-aware development style the posting requires.

---
recommendedSkills: **Node.js + Fastify REST API development:** This is the single highest-impact gap — the posting lists it as a hard requirement alongside React. Build a standalone Fastify service with TypeScript, Zod schema validation, and OpenAPI output. Given David's Python API background, the concepts are identical; learning Fastify's plugin model and TypeScript typing discipline should take 4–8 weeks to reach working proficiency.

**Kafka basics and event-driven patterns:** Kafka is the integration backbone of the NBA pipeline. Standing up a local Kafka instance, building a producer/consumer in Node.js/TypeScript, and understanding consumer groups and at-least-once vs. exactly-once delivery would cover the core of what the posting requires — roughly 2–4 weeks of focused study and a small project.

**TanStack Query + TanStack Router:** These are the preferred React state/routing libraries for this team. Adding them to the Community Center Rentals or a new project would demonstrate modern React architecture alignment. 1–2 weeks to productive use given existing React fluency.

**Prisma or Drizzle ORM (TypeScript):** The posting lists both as preferred. Adding Drizzle to the Community Center Rentals project (which already uses Neon PostgreSQL) would simultaneously strengthen the project entry and demonstrate the skill — 1 week to integrate.

**OpenAPI / contract-first API design:** The posting calls out contract-first principles and schema validation as a hard requirement. Learning to write OpenAPI 3.x specs and generate TypeScript types from them (e.g., with `openapi-typescript`) is a 1-week investment that would make every Node.js API David builds immediately more credible for this role. ---
recommendedCourses: **Node.js, Express, MongoDB & More: The Complete Bootcamp** — Udemy (Jonas Schmedtmann). Covers Node.js fundamentals and REST API design; pivot the capstone to use Fastify + PostgreSQL to match the posting's stack. Directly addresses the primary hard gap.

**Apache Kafka for Beginners — Learn Apache Kafka for DevOps** — Udemy (Stephane Maarek). Maarek's Kafka series is widely recognized; covers producers, consumers, topics, partitions, and exactly-once semantics. Addresses the Kafka workflow-integration requirement.

**Designing RESTful APIs** — Coursera / UC Davis. Covers contract-first design, OpenAPI specification, and API versioning — maps directly to the posting's "contract-first principles and schema validation" requirement.

**AWS Certified Developer – Associate** — Amazon Web Services. Validates Lambda, API Gateway, and cloud-native development patterns David already uses; adds credibility on the cloud deployment side and is achievable quickly given his existing AWS CCP and hands-on Lambda work. ---
recommendedExperience: **Build a Node.js/Fastify microservice at Rice or as a side project:** Replace one of the Python/Flask API endpoints with a TypeScript Fastify service backed by PostgreSQL, complete with Zod validation, an OpenAPI spec, and Jest integration tests. This produces a real, demoable artifact that directly answers the posting's primary hard requirement.

**Add a Kafka-based event bus to the Community Center Rentals project:** Publish booking-confirmed and booking-cancelled events to a local Kafka topic and build a consumer that updates a read-model or sends notifications. This produces a portfolio example of exactly-once side-effect handling — one of the posting's explicit success indicators.

**Migrate Community Center Rentals ORM to Drizzle:** Replacing raw SQL with Drizzle ORM adds a preferred-qualification credential to a project that already demonstrates the full TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Redis stack the posting wants.

**Seek PHI/compliance-adjacent work at Rice:** The IT department likely handles FERPA-regulated student data. Documenting data-handling practices, access controls, and audit logging in a compliance-conscious way on current projects would give David a concrete answer when the healthcare-regulated-environment question comes up in interviews. ---

Senior Full Stack Engineer — Northwind Health

recommendations.scoreRationale:
David meets the core hard requirements solidly: 5+ years of software engineering, production React experience (including TypeScript via Next.js), PostgreSQL schema design, CI/CD pipelines, and enterprise workflow/access-control patterns. The score is held down by two meaningful gaps against hard requirements: the posting explicitly demands strong Node.js/TypeScript backend API development as a primary skill, and David's backend work has been primarily in Python (Flask/Django) and Salesforce Apex rather than Node.js/Fastify — TypeScript backend is present in Next.js server components but not standalone REST API services. Additionally, Kafka and event-driven architecture are listed as a workflow integration requirement he has no direct experience with.

---
resumeRecommendations: **Reframe the Community Center Rentals project explicitly around state integrity and idempotency:** The posting's success indicators are "state transitions are precise and deterministic" and "side effects occur exactly once." The project already has advisory locks and transaction-level re-checks — use that language verbatim. The current description buries the lead.

**Add TypeScript as a named, primary language:** The master resume lists it implicitly through Next.js but never calls it out in the skills section. The posting uses "TypeScript" 11 times — it must appear prominently in the languages row of the skills table and in bullets for Community Center Rentals and the Salesforce LWC work.

**Quantify the Salesforce workflow scope more precisely:** "60+ flows" and "10,000 active users" are already present — good. Add the number of API integrations, average daily transactions, or SLA/uptime metrics if known. The posting values reliability and scale; numbers make that concrete.

**Use the posting's vocabulary in the Rice bullets:** Replace generic phrasing like "maintained cloud APIs" with terms the posting uses: "designed data models," "governed workflows," "versioned configurations," "contract-based integrations." ATS and human reviewers will both respond to keyword alignment.

**Surface the AWS Bedrock / LLM integration work explicitly:** The applicant context notes recent production LLM work with Bedrock. If any Bedrock integration exists at Rice or in a project, add a dedicated bullet — the posting's success indicator "AI-driven tooling decreases defect rates and expedites debugging" signals the team is actively using AI tooling, and this would be a strong differentiator.
